antidotes.why: Think of strength, not of weakness.
Someone reminds Hanuman who he is when he feels small.
Have faith because you are more than what has happened.
What you are is not small.

steps.en: what our thoughts have made us

chains.summary: Our thoughts make us what we are. If you think you are weak, you will be weak. The remedy for weakness is thinking of strength, not brooding over weakness.
chains.title: We are what our thoughts have made us

verses.sa: We are what our thoughts have made us; so take care of what you think.
If you think yourselves weak, weak you will be; if you think yourselves strong, strong you will be;
The remedy for weakness is not brooding over weakness, but thinking of strength.

chains.summary: A person is poor when his craving is large. When the mind is content, there is no distinction between rich and poor.
chains.title: Who is rich, who is poor

verses.m: We are content here with bark garments, you with silk; the contentment is equal, and the difference makes no difference. He is poor whose craving is vast. When the mind is content, who is rich and who is poor?
verses.sa: वयमिह परितुष्टा वल्कलैस्त्वं दुकूलैः सम इव परितोषो निर्विशेषो विशेषः । स तु भवतु दरिद्रो यस्य तृष्णा विशाला मनसि च परितुष्टे कोऽर्थवान्को दरिद्रः ॥

verses.m: Those always delighted by contentment have joy that is undivided; the others, minds crowded with greed for money, never kill their craving. So for whom did fate make wealth, and what kind of place is it? Mount Meru, whose golden glory ends in itself, does not appeal to me.
verses.sa: ये सन्तोषनिरन्तरप्रमुदितास्तेषां न भिन्ना मुदो ये त्वन्ये धनलुब्धसंकुलधियस्तेषां न तृष्णा हता । इत्थं कस्य कृते कृतः स विधिना कीदृक्पदं सम्पदां स्वात्मन्येव समाप्तहेममहिमा मेरुर्न मे रोचते ॥

chains.summary: Craving leads a person like a bullock on a knotted rope and shrinks even the wise and brave to a blade of grass. Letting go of anxious thought is its cure.
chains.title: Craving on a rope

verses.m: Knotted inside the body and hard to cut, craving drags a person along the way a rope drags a bullock.
verses.sa: अन्तर्ग्रथितया देहे सर्वदुश्छेदयाऽनया । रज्ज्वेवाशु बलीवर्दस्तृष्णया वाह्यते जनः ॥

verses.m: People let go of all their sorrow when they let go of worry. Giving up worry is called the cure for the sickness of craving.
verses.sa: लोकोऽयमखिलं दुःखं चिन्तयोज्झितयोज्झति । तृष्णाविषूचिकामन्त्रश्चिन्तात्यागो हि कथ्यते ॥

verses.m: Even a man who is wise, brave and steady as Mount Meru, the best of men, craving alone turns into a blade of grass in an instant.
verses.sa: अपि मेरुसमं प्राज्ञमपि शूरमपि स्थिरम् । तृणीकरोति तृष्णैका निमेषेण नरोत्तमम् ॥

depicts.m: I somehow put up with the taunts of the wicked while trying to please them; I held back my tears and laughed with an empty heart; I folded my hands even before people whose minds were numbed by money. Hope, futile hope, how much more will you make me dance?
depicts.sa: खलालापाः सोढाः कथमपि तदाराधनपरैः निगृह्यान्तर्बाष्पं हसितमपि शून्येन मनसा । कृतो वित्तस्तम्भप्रतिहतधियामञ्जलिरपि त्वमाशे मोघाशे किमपरमतो नर्तयसि माम् ॥
depicts.why: Shows folding hands before people numbed by money.

depicts.m: O heart, why do you enter into weariness, day after day trying to please the minds of others in so many ways, to win their favour? When you are at peace within, your own clear resolve rises by itself like a cluster of wish-granting gems: what wish of yours would it not fulfil?
depicts.sa: परेषां चेतांसि प्रतिदिवसमाराध्य बहुधा प्रसादं किं नेतुं विशसि हृदय क्लेशकलितम् । प्रसन्ने त्वय्यन्तः स्वयमुदितचिन्तामणिगणो विविक्तः संकल्पः किमभिलषितं पुष्यति न ते ॥

depicts.m: A person who is straightforward, and modest because of it, is taken for weak by small-minded people, and they push him around.
depicts.sa: आर्जवेन नरं युक्तमार्जवात्सव्यपत्रपम् / अशक्तं मन्यमानास्तु धर्षयन्ति कुबुद्धयः

depicts.m: He will set right everything about me, he whose kindness never tires of being kind. Ram is a good master and I am a poor servant, yet the ocean of compassion looks at it from his own side and cares for me.
depicts.sa: मोरि सुधारिहि सो सब भाँती। जासु कृपा नहिं कृपाँ अघाती॥ राम सुस्वामि कुसेवकु मोसो। निज दिसि देखि दयानिधि पोसो ॥
depicts.why: Shows him calling himself a bad servant.

depicts.m: 'Will Ram, my master, with his brother, meet me as he would his own servant? There is no firm trust in my heart; no devotion, detachment or wisdom in my mind; no good company, no yoga, chanting or sacrifice, no steady love for his lotus feet. But the ocean of compassion has one habit: the one who has no other refuge is dear to him.'
depicts.sa: सहित अनुज मोहि राम गोसाईं। मिलिहहिं निज सेवक की नाईं॥ मोरे जियँ भरोस दृढ़ नाहीं। भगति बिरति न ग्यान मन माहीं ॥ नहिं सतसंग जोग जप जागा। नहिं दृढ़ चरन कमल अनुरागा॥ एक बानि करुनानिधान की। सो प्रिय जाकें गति न आन की ॥

depicts.m: Hearing your good name with my own ears I have come, Lord, breaker of the fear of the world. Save me, save me, remover of distress, Raghubir, whose refuge brings joy.
depicts.sa: श्रवन सुजसु सुनि आयउँ प्रभु भंजन भव भीर। त्राहि त्राहि आरति हरन सरन सुखद रघुबीर ॥
depicts.why: Arrives with nothing but what he has heard.

depicts.m: You are kind and I am in need; you give and I am a beggar. I am a known wrongdoer and you lift heaps of wrong. Lord, you shelter those who have no one, and who has less than I do? No one hurts as I do, and no one heals hurt as you do. You are the infinite, I a small life; you the master, I the servant. Father and mother, teacher and friend: you wish me well in every way. There are many bonds between us; take whichever one pleases you. Only let Tulsi, somehow, find shelter at your feet.
depicts.sa: तू दयालु, दीन हौं, तू दानि, हौं भिखारी । हौं प्रसिद्ध पातकी, तू पाप-पुंज-हारी॥ नाथ तू अनाथको, अनाथ कौन मोसो। मो समान आरत नहिं, आरतिहर तोसो॥ ब्रह्म तू, हौं जीव, तू है ठाकुर, हौं चेरो। तात-मात, गुरु-सखा, तू सब बिधि हितु मेरो॥ तोहिं मोहिं नाते अनेक, मानियै जो भावै। ज्यों त्यों तुलसी कृपालु! चरन-सरन पावै॥
depicts.why: Depicts none so helpless or afflicted as he.

depicts.m: What weighs on my mind is this: I, so poor here, cannot do anything equal in return for the one who brought me such good news.
depicts.sa: इदं तु मम दीनस्य मनो भूयः प्रकर्षति। यदिहास्य प्रियाख्यातुर्न कुर्मि सदृशं प्रियम् ॥
depicts.why: Names the smallness of having nothing to give.

gloss: Thinking oneself low or not enough. As an affliction the texts oppose it (never look down on yourself, MBh 3.32.58); as a devotional mood before God, Tulsidas and Surdas voice it and are lifted in it.

heals.m: Everyone's faith follows their nature, Bharata. A person is made of faith; as a person's faith is, so is that person.
heals.sa: सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत । श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः ॥

heals.m: A person should never look down on himself. The one who despises himself never finds real prosperity.
heals.r: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
heals.sa: न त्वेवात्माऽवमन्तव्यः पुरुषेण कदाचन / न ह्यात्मपरिभूतस् भूतिर्भवति शोभना

heals.m: Listen, Hanuman: don't let your heart feel small. You are twice as dear to me as Lakshman. Everyone calls me impartial, yet the one who serves me is dear to me, because he has no other refuge.
heals.sa: सुनु कपि जियँ मानसि जनि ऊना। तैं मम प्रिय लछिमन ते दूना॥ समदरसी मोहि कह सब कोऊ। सेवक प्रिय अनन्य गति सोऊ ॥
heals.why: He is told not to count himself less.

heals.m: That which is the subtle essence: this whole world has it as its self. That is the truth. That is the self. That you are, Shvetaketu. 'Teach me more, sir.' 'So be it, dear one.'
heals.sa: स य एषोऽणिमैतदात्म्यमिदꣳ सर्वं तत्सत्यꣳ स आत्मा तत्त्वमसि श्वेतकेतो इति भूय एव मा भगवान्विज्ञापयत्विति तथा सोम्येति होवाच ॥
heals.why: Names the root where smallness does not reach.

heals.sa: Come up, O lions, and shake off the delusion that you are sheep;
The remedy for weakness is not brooding over weakness, but thinking of strength.

heals.m: In you, the boundless ocean, let the waves of the world rise or fall by their own nature. You neither grow nor shrink.
heals.sa: त्वय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ विश्ववीचिः स्वभावतः । उदेतु वास्तमायातु न ते वृद्धिर्न वा क्षतिः ॥
heals.why: Worth does not shrink with a loss of role or status.

heals.m: One who watches his own active body as if it were someone else's: how could praise or blame disturb such a large-hearted person?
heals.sa: चेष्टमानं शरीरं स्वं पश्यत्यन्यशरीरवत् । संस्तवे चापि निन्दायां कथं क्षुभ्येत् महाशयः ॥
heals.why: Shows blame landing on the body-mind being watched, not on the watcher.

hero.m: My nature is stricken by weakness and my mind is confused about what is right. I ask you: tell me for certain what is best for me. I am your student; I have come to you, teach me.
hero.sa: कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावःपृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसंमूढचेताः । यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्िचतं ब्रूहि तन्मेशिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम् ॥

loci.m: My nature is stricken by weakness and my mind is confused about what is right. I ask you: tell me for certain what is best for me. I am your student; I have come to you, teach me.
loci.sa: कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावःपृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसंमूढचेताः । यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्िचतं ब्रूहि तन्मेशिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम् ॥

loci.m: There is no one as poor as I am, and no friend of the poor like you, Raghubir. Thinking this over, jewel of the Raghus, take away the heavy fear of the world.
loci.sa: मो सम दीन न दीन हित तुम्ह समान रघुबीर। अस बिचारि रघुबंस मनि हरहु बिषम भव भीर ॥

practices.m: Learn it by bowing down, by questioning, and by service. Those who are wise and have seen the truth will teach you that knowledge.
practices.sa: तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया । उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥
practices.why: Shows humility before a teacher who has seen the truth.

practices.m: One who, by comparison with himself, sees the same everywhere, Arjuna, whether in pleasure or in pain, is considered the highest yogi.
practices.sa: आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन । सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं सः योगी परमो मतः ॥
practices.why: Shows others' pain is known by one's own.

practices.m: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
practices.sa: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥

practices.m: Good company takes dullness from the mind, sprinkles truth into speech, raises one's dignity, removes wrongdoing, clears the heart and spreads one's good name in every direction. Tell me, what does good company not do for a person?
practices.sa: जाड्यं धियो हरति सिञ्चति वाचि सत्यं मानोन्नतिं दिशति पापमपाकरोति । चेतः प्रसादयति दिक्षु तनोति कीर्तिं सत्सङ्गतिः कथय किं न करोति पुंसाम् ॥

practices.m: Friend chataka, listen carefully for a moment. Many clouds live in the sky, but not all are alike. Some drench the earth with rain; some only thunder for nothing. Do not speak pleading words before every cloud you see.
practices.sa: रे रे चातक सावधानमनसा मित्र क्षणं श्रूयताम् अम्भोदा बहवो वसन्ति गगने सर्वेऽपि नैकादृशाः । केचिद्वृष्टिभिरार्द्रयन्ति धरणीं गर्जन्ति केचिद्वृथा यं यं पश्यसि तस्य तस्य पुरतो मा ब्रूहि दीनं वचः ॥
practices.why: Keeps asking for those who can and will help.

practices.m: A wicked person should be avoided, even if adorned with learning. Is a snake any less frightening because it wears a jewel?
practices.sa: दुर्जनः परिहर्तव्यो विद्ययालङ्कृतोऽपि सन् । मणिना भूषितः सर्पः किमसौ न भयङ्करः ॥

practices.m: Do not wound others where it hurts, do not speak cruelly, do not take from those who have less. Never say words that make another person flinch; such words are scorching and lead to dark places.
practices.sa: नारुतुदः स्यान्न नृशंसवादी / न हीनतः परमभ्याददीत / ययाऽस्य वाचा पर उद्विजेत / न तां वदेदुशतिं पापलोक्याम्
practices.why: Shows one feeling the other's flinch before speaking.

practices.m: Provisions for the wilderness of life, medicine that cuts the bonds of the world, rescue from sorrow and grief: the two syllables 'Ha-ri'.
practices.why: Trust is cultivated in two syllables.

stories.l: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.
stories.s: Krishna challenges Arjuna's despair. Arjuna admits he is confused about what is right, cannot tell which choice is better, and asks Krishna to teach him.
stories.t: Krishna and Arjuna on Arjuna's faint-heartedness

stories.l: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.
stories.s: Arjuna fears that one who falls short is lost like a torn cloud. Krishna promises that no one who does good comes to ruin; past effort carries forward and they strive again.
stories.t: What becomes of one who falls from yoga

stories.l: When the mind is content, nobody is richer than you.
stories.s: An ascetic tells a king who ignores him that learning equals wealth, that contentment in bark equals contentment in silk, and that pride over a few towns is a fever.
stories.t: Vairagyashatakam: Dialogue between the ascetic and the king

stories.l: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.
stories.s: The poet confesses everything he did for money and approval: digging for treasure, flattering kings, forcing laughter. He ends with the famous lines that pleasures consumed us and craving never aged, and hope pictured as a river.
